latest_final: The "courses" were not academic classes but the food courses—the dishes—of a University of Hong Kong residential-hall high-table dinner, a one-evening celebration. Before the dinner there was a deadline by which the student had to choose his dishes (his meal courses for the dinner), which made the situation sound exactly like registering for university courses. At the dinner the meal was served course by course (a multi-course menu in sequence), and the student, along with the other attending guests at their own places, ate the dishes. The student ate some of what he had chosen but could not finish it all; the remaining courses he had selected were thrown away/discarded once the single-evening dinner ended. So by the end of that evening all of "his courses" were gone—some eaten, the rest discarded—with no theft, system glitch, cancellation, or lost reservation. The only trick is linguistic: "choosing courses before the deadline" and "all my courses were gone in one evening" refer here to picking and then consuming (and discarding the leftovers of) dinner dishes at a hall high-table dinner, not to a course-registration disaster.
